extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in international/war news
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting on military, diplomatic and economic developments during the Scandinavian/WWII campaign for a newspaper audience; composed of datelined, agency-attributed dispatches and official communiques. Emphasizes timeliness, source attribution and cautious treatment of unconfirmed details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution to authoritative sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and name authoritative sources when reporting claims (examples in text: 'Authoritative sources said', 'The War Office said', 'Air Ministry communique said', 'The French War Ministry said').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute operational and strategic claims to ministries, military spokesmen or official communiques rather than reporting them as undisputed fact; the article repeatedly uses phrases like 'Authoritative sources said', 'The War Office said', 'An informed source said'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide complete and timely information to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters should supply full, timely information to readers; the piece notes a criticism that 'the public was not getting complete news.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge public demand for answers and aim to address questions that 'are troubling the public mind,' as the article paraphrases public criticism: 'the public "is prepared—much more than the government" ... the questions being asked events in Norway "are troubling public mind".'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use datelines and agency attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Include location, date and wire-service attribution at the start of dispatches (examples: 'LONDON, April 26 (A. P.).—', 'By The Associated Press', 'By The Canadian Press').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datelines and agency labels orient readers to where and by whom a report was filed and are used consistently across the dispatches on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report uncertainty and avoid asserting unconfirmed details
rubrics_metrics.description: When information is incomplete or unconfirmed, state that explicitly (examples: 'no reports of allied losses had been received yet', 'it was not known whether the expeditionary troops had support from artillery and aircraft guns', 'it is not known whether the Germans were bound for Sweden or to reinforce German troops in Norway').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cautious phrasing to flag unknowns and avoid definitive assertions about troop movements, losses or intentions until verified; the article models this by presenting uncertainty prominently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on official communiques for military operational details
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Ministry/War Office/Air Ministry communiques and official military statements to report on operations and losses (example: 'The Air Ministry communique said: "Vigorous offensive action by large numbers of Air Force aircraft..."').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite and quote official communiques for numbers and operational claims (aircraft missing, ships attacked, artillery actions), while still attributing them to the issuing authority rather than treating them as independent verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include multiple angles (military, diplomatic, economic, domestic) in wartime coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Wartime reporting on this page spans battlefield actions, diplomatic maneuvers, economic measures and domestic politics (examples include military actions in Norway, Anglo-Swedish diplomatic assurances, trade/blockade discussions, and Italian parliamentary speeches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide readers a broad view of events by combining operational reports with diplomatic context and economic implications—as this compilation does—so that the war's multiple dimensions are conveyed.
